## Critique
- claim-1: Artifact `3129cd3441577148a7881a2840a1b14c9448350e2a6e2e94f6f88aa21a625891` supports the listed bases, complete low-degree Pieri matrices, complementary minors with determinants \(1,1,-1,-1,1\), coordinate matrices \(I_6,C\), and determinants \(1,-1\). However, the specialist output omits the logical step showing that the selected primitive row lattices equal the complete Pieri row lattices, and it does not display row combinations deriving the five relations. Thus the requested certificate is not yet explicit as written.
- claim-2: This is a correct scope limitation. It neither repairs nor weakens the bounded certificate.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Let \(R_d\) be the complete row lattice of the displayed \(M_d\), and \(L_d\) the lattice generated by the selected rows. The complementary minors on the non-\(B\) columns have determinants \(1,1,-1,-1,1\), so
  \[
  \mathbb Z^{C_d}/L_d\cong\mathbb Z^{B_d}.
  \]
  The accepted complete-matrix ranks are \(0,1,3,6,10=|C_d|-|B_d|\); hence \(\operatorname{rank}R_d=\operatorname{rank}L_d\). Since \(R_d/L_d\) embeds in the free group \(\mathbb Z^{C_d}/L_d\) and has rank zero, \(R_d=L_d\). Therefore
  \[
  B=(\bar s_{22},\bar s_{32},\bar s_{42},\bar s_{33},\bar s_{43},\bar s_{44})
  \]
  is an integral quotient basis. If \(r_{d,k}\) denotes row \(k\) of the displayed degree-\(d\) matrix, the required relations follow from
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
  r_{5,1}&=s_{32}+s_{221},\\
  r_{6,3}-r_{6,1}&=s_{222}-s_{33},\\
  r_{6,2}-r_{6,3}&=s_{2211}-s_{42},\\
  r_{7,1}-r_{7,8}+r_{7,4}&=s_{43}+s_{2221},\\
  r_{8,11}-r_{8,14}+r_{8,2}-r_{8,15}-r_{8,1}&=s_{2222}-s_{44}.
  \end{aligned}
  \]
  The replacement should then state the column convention and display \(I_6\), \(C\), with determinants \(1,-1\).

## Required revisions
- Add the preceding row-lattice equality argument and explicit five row combinations.
- Explicitly define both ordered families, \(B\), and the row/column orientation of their coordinate matrices.
- Conclude explicitly that this quotient-coordinate certificate is established, while making no parent-theorem claim.
